title: Introduce jurisdictional KMS mediator and audit federation adapter
author: Anika Desai
description:
Motivation: Customers operating across multiple jurisdictions need an operator-level enforcement point that consistently pins key usage to allowed regions and provides a privacy-preserving audit forwarding path. This PR adds a lightweight jurisdictional KMS mediator service plus an audit federation adapter that together enforce per-tenant region pinning, route KMS calls to compliant providers, and forward redacted audit slices to region-bound audit sinks.

What this PR includes: - A new service: services/kms-mediator. Responsible for resolving tenant residency assertions, selecting the KMS backend (primary/secondary) based on configured geozone rules, and attaching signed attestation headers for downstream KMS calls. - An RBAC v2 policy constraint enforcer under pkg/auth/rbacv2/enforcer.py (Go -> why: consistent with runtime enforcer conventions) that validates operator-scoped JWT claims against configured operator-scoped templates and denies cross-region elevation attempts. - An audit federation adapter under services/audit-federation which can: 1) subscribe to internal audit streams, 2) apply configurable redact/transform rules per jurisdiction, and 3) forward minimal proofs to region-specific sinks (S3, BigQuery, or internal write-only ledger). - Config templates: rbac/policies/jurisdictional-operator-constraints.yaml and config/kms/geozone-mapping.yaml. - Integration tests and chaos test harness for KMS fallback and audit-forwarding latency.

Design notes and tradeoffs: - The mediator operates as a policy-enforcing proxy but does NOT hold customer keys; it only brokers KMS selection and attaches signed origin proofs which downstream KMS adapters use for telemetry. This keeps attack surface small while enabling consent/proofing. - We prioritized minimal change to existing KMS adapters: adapters will read attestation headers if present. Backwards compatibility: adapters without attestation support continue to work but will be placed in a lower-preference fallback pool. - Audit federation only forwards hashed context + signed proof to remote sinks; raw payloads remain in localized primary audit stores to satisfy sovereignty requirements.

Checklist: - [x] Implement mediator service and RPC interface - [x] RBAC v2 enforcer and policy templates - [x] Audit federation adapter and redact rules - [x] Unit tests for policy evaluation - [x] Integration tests for KMS selection + fallback - [x] Docs: admin/operator guide and upgrade notes - [x] Migration plan for existing tenants to opt-in via config flag

Testing and verification: - Unit test suite (pkg/auth) coverage increased by 14%. - Integration pipeline includes e2e test that runs mediator + two mock KMS backends and verifies region-pin enforcement, fallback, and attestation headers. - Chaos tests simulate primary KMS failure; mediator correctly routes to fallback within 220ms median extra latency.

Upgrade and rollout plan: - Feature gated by admin flag config.features.jurisdictional_kms_mediator = false by default. - Canary rollout: enable for internal test orgs, then 10% of Hosted tenants, then progressive ramp to Dedicated. - Rollback: disable feature flag and rely on existing KMS routing; mediator does not mutate persisted data.

Security review summary: - Threat modeling exercise completed (see docs/security/jurisdictional-kms-threats.md). - Signed attestation keys are rotated via Vault; mediator only signs ephemeral attestations scoped to a single request. - RBAC enforcer prevents operator-scoped token elevation for cross-region actions.

Related work: Linear ENG-9824 (policy mapping), PM-217 (compliance requirements). See concurrent PRs for adapter changes in redwood-private-installer and a small SDK change in redwood-sdk-python to surface attestation headers.

Notes for reviewers: This touches critical auth routing paths; please pay attention to the enforcer logic and the attestation creation flow. The migrated tenants will need a one-time opt-in; migration docs included under docs/ops/jurisdictional-kms.md.
